summary: Best verified state 158e86783f0ad7d4: 1.071x over the baseline (240 pairs, CI [1.066, 1.077], 0.1171 ms vs 0.1253 ms). Most of that is NOT machine-level: relaunching amdclang's unchanged code with 512 threads per workgroup instead of 1024 (8 waves, 2 rounds per thread at the bench shape; state c58877b909110425) is already ~1.05-1.06x. The machine-level part, measured directly with compare(c58877b909110425, 158e86783f0ad7d4, 240 pairs), is 1.021x (CI [1.017, 1.025]): a straight-line fast path for rounds<=4 that issues all rounds' masked input loads before one wait, keeps them in v[24:39] across the LDS reduction so the second pass does not re-read the input, puts the weight loads in flight together, and stores without a loop; rounds>4 falls back to amdclang's loops. Case: memory floor. Each element is read once and written once (the second input read in the baseline is a cache hit and removing it measured parity); reference headroom 1.17-1.20, final headroom 1.12; a probe with the whole cross-wave reduction and barrier removed was only 0.8% faster. 1.5x is out of reach without moving fewer bytes, and there are none to save. Correctness note: the battery at the shipped launch only ever runs rounds=1, so I verified the multi-round fast path (rounds=3 with a tail, eb8e69637301f073) and the fallback (rounds=8, ced1eadc5fbb2e07) with test-only relaunches of the same code; both pass 77/77.

friction: edit() text does not accept label lines (ops[3]: bad mnemonic '.Lslow:'), so any edit that adds a branch target forces edit_ir with the whole 220-instruction body retyped. A 'split block here / new label' op would have saved most of the effort; I first worked around it by zeroing exec around a load (s_cselect_b64 exec, exec, 0).

The battery at the manifest launch never runs rounds>1 for this kernel (D4 <= 257 with block min(1024, D4)), yet the bench shape under a 512-thread launch runs rounds=2 and D4 > 1024 would run it at the shipped launch. A multi-round path can pass check untested. I had to create test-only relaunch states (block min(96, D4) and min(32, D4)) to cover it; a battery shape with D4 > 1024, or a way to run the battery under an alternate launch without creating states, would close this.

unroll_loads refuses masked multi-block loops ('no single-block loop'), which is exactly what amdclang emits for this library-style per-thread strided loop (mask, saveexec, branch, load, wait). The hand version was worth +11% at 4 rounds and +2% at 2 rounds.

It is unclear from the tools whether a relaunch (block size change on amdclang's unchanged code) counts as machine-level or as amdclang's build. I measured the control myself (c58877b909110425) to separate the two; bench could report this split when a state differs from the baseline in both launch and code.
No documented answer on whether a global_load with exec == 0 increments vmcnt; I avoided a pipelined vmcnt(3) wait and used vmcnt(0) because of it. arch('waitcnt') could state it.
lessons: fi_rmsnorm (B=16384, d=4096, 268 MB read + 268 MB written) is at the memory floor: reference headroom 1.17-1.20, best state 1.12. Removing the whole cross-wave LDS reduction and its barrier in a probe gained 0.8%; removing the second barrier and the smem[0] round trip in a correct state was parity (1.005).

Keeping the input in registers across the reduction instead of re-reading it in the update pass was parity here (1.003), unlike mo_t5_layernorm / kda_step (1.7x). The re-read is of the 1 KB the same wave just loaded and hits cache; the lever only pays when the second read is cold.

Workgroup size is the main knob for one-workgroup-per-row kernels with 16 KB rows: threads per workgroup 1024 (16 waves, 1 round) 1.00; 768 0.92; 512 (8 waves, 2 rounds) 1.06; 352 1.06; 256 0.94 with amdclang's loop and 1.05 with all rounds' loads in flight; 128 0.86. 8 waves per workgroup beat 16 even though each thread then loops.

Loads in flight for a per-thread strided loop: +2.1% at 2 rounds (compare, 240 pairs, CI [1.017, 1.025]) and about +11% at 4 rounds (0.943 -> 1.047). The gain scales with the number of serial waits removed, but did not move the optimum geometry.
coarsen factor 2: 1.026 on the 16-wave launch, but it made the 8-wave launch worse (1.062 -> 1.026). Coarsening and a smaller workgroup do not combine.
A load can be made conditional without a branch or a new label: s_mov_b64 sN, exec; s_cmp; s_cselect_b64 exec, exec, 0; load; s_mov_b64 exec, sN. Passed static_check and the battery.
To test a rounds>1 path that the battery shapes never reach, relaunch the same code with a smaller block expression (min(96, D4) gave rounds=3 with a tail at D4=250) and run check on that state.

session.final:
The session is finished and the report is recorded. The best verified state is `158e86783f0ad7d4`, 1.071x over the baseline (240 pairs, CI [1.066, 1.077]) — well short of the 1.5x target, which is out of reach here.

- **Why 1.5x is out of reach:** the kernel is at the memory floor. Each element is read once and written once, the baseline's headroom is 1.17–1.20, and a probe with the whole cross-wave reduction removed was only 0.8% faster.
- **Where the 1.07x comes from:** mostly the launch, not the machine code. Running amdclang's unchanged code with 512 threads per workgroup instead of 1024 (state `c58877b909110425`) accounts for the bulk — about 1.06x measured with my parity edits on top; the control itself was not timed against the baseline.
- **Machine-level gain:** 1.021x over that launch-only control (compare at 240 pairs, CI [1.017, 1.025]). It comes from a loop-free fast path for up to four rounds: all input loads issued before one wait, the input kept in registers across the reduction, and the weight loads in flight together. More rounds fall back to amdclang's loops.
- **What did not pay:**
  - Keeping the input in registers at the original launch was parity (1.003).
  - Dropping the second barrier was parity (1.005).
  - `coarsen` gave 1.026 at the original launch but made the 512-thread launch worse.
  - Other workgroup sizes: 768 threads 0.92, 256 threads 0.94 with amdclang's loop (1.05 with my fast path), 128 threads 0.86; 352 threads tied with 512.

The battery at the shipped launch only ever runs one round per thread, so it never exercises the multi-round code that the bench shape uses. I covered it with two test-only relaunches of the same code (three rounds with a tail, and the eight-round fallback); both pass 77/77.

The harness may credit the launch change to amdclang and measure my state against that; in that case the result is the 1.02x.
